movesets.name: Aurora Veil
movesets.description:
With its unique combination of Aurora Veil, Snow Warning, and a good Speed tier, Alolan Ninetales establishes itself as a premiere lead for setting Aurora Veil, giving it the advantage over fellow dual screens setters like Grimmsnarl and Deoxys-S, which require two turns instead to set up. Encore shuts down setup sweepers that try to take advantage of Alolan Ninetales's mediocre offensive presence like Kingambit and punishes defensive Pokemon like Ting-Lu, Garganacl, and Corviknight, giving Alolan Ninetales's teammates free opportunities to set up. Freeze-Dry threatens common leads like Landorus-T, Hisuian Samurott, and Gliscor as well as Pelipper, which otherwise removes Alolan Ninetales's snow unthreatened. Freeze-Dry can also target certain threats like Ogerpon-W and Walking Wake. Moonblast serves as a stronger secondary STAB option to slam threats like Darkrai, Zamazenta, and Weavile that Freeze-Dry cannot while hitting Hisuian Samurott slightly harder. Snowscape allows Alolan Ninetales to reset snow in the face of weather setters Torkoal, Ninetales, Pelipper, and Tyranitar, ensuring both Aurora Veil and the advantage in the weather wars. Roar is an option to improve the mirror matchup against offensive teams, as it can stop setup sweepers like Terastallized Dragonite and Zamazenta more reliably in cases where Encore couldn't. Moreover, forcing in the Booster Energy users into the field essentially wastes the item if they're not ready to sweep yet. Though Alolan Ninetales rarely wants to Terastallize, Tera Water is run to shed its Fire and Steel weaknesses, flipping the matchup on Pokemon like Iron Moth, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown. Tera Ghost is also an option to emergency check a boosted IronPress Zamazenta, especially with Encore.

With its invaluable ability to set dual screens in one turn, Alolan Ninetales cements itself as a lead for hyper offense teams. One sweeper that pairs exceptionally well with Alolan Ninetales is Kyurem, as its Dragon Dance set heavily appreciates both Aurora Veil and snow extending its already solid bulk to absurd levels. Other setup sweepers like Zamazenta, Kingambit, and Raging Bolt similarly enjoy Aurora Veil, able to boost with near impunity then crush the opposing team. In particular, Bulk Up Great Tusk is an excellent teammate for its added entry hazard removal in Rapid Spin, which Aurora Veil teams can otherwise struggle with. Rillaboom combines Grassy Terrain's recovery with Aurora Veil to allow even more opportunities for its teammates to set up with ease, which is especially useful for those weak to Earthquake like the aforementioned Raging Bolt and Kingambit. However, Alolan Ninetales's biggest foe, Cinderace, resists both of its STAB moves and can steal Aurora Veil with Court Change. Other major threats include Iron Moth and Steel-types like Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Scizor, which similarly ignore Alolan Ninetales's attacks, can threaten an OHKO, and, in Iron Moth's case, can set up a Substitute freely. Thus, a great partner is Manaphy, which is able to shrug off any Steel- and Fire-type attacks while synergizing well with Aurora Veil, especially for its Double Dance set. Iron Moth easily boosts on Cinderace and threatens Steel-types, as well as snowballing through sun and Sticky Web teams that would otherwise give Alolan Ninetales trouble; Aurora Veil allows Iron Moth to take a hit or two, which is especially useful for the Substitute variants. Dragonite can serve as a useful check to Iron Moth, offensive Cinderace, and other offensive threats with its powerful Extreme Speed. Another Pokemon to watch out for is Corviknight, which can remove Aurora Veil with Defog, so teammates like the aforementioned Iron Moth and Raging Bolt are useful to pressure it from ever entering the field and using Defog freely.

strategies.overview: Alolan Ninetales carves out a niche for itself thanks to the combination of its high Speed and being the only relevant Pokemon with access to both Aurora Veil and Snow Warning. In conjunction with Encore to cripple slower Pokemon that often use status moves like Bisharp and Cresselia, this lets it support its teammates fairly well. Its high Speed lets it outrun foes like Krookodile and Terrakion, and the Defense boost provided by snow lets it take priority moves from slower wallbreakers like Mimikyu and Crawdaunt. Additionally, Alolan Ninetales can act as a rare specially offensive Ice-type with Nasty Plot to punch holes in teams. However, its typing leaves it with a myriad of common weaknesses, including to Stealth Rock; this often forces Alolan Ninetales to choose between extending the duration of its snow or not getting nailed by entry hazards. Without Terastallization, offensive Alolan Ninetales sets lack the coverage to muscle through the Steel-types that resist both of its STAB moves, like Jirachi and Registeel, which limits the flexibility of its team. Alolan Ninetales's Special Attack is also relatively low, meaning without sufficient boosts it's walled by Pokemon like Volcanion and Hisuian Goodra. Additionally, while Alolan Ninetales's Speed is solid, it's still outsped by common Pokemon like Gengar and Barraskewda.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

On the Nasty Plot set, Aurora Veil can be run over Encore in order to bolster Alolan Ninetales's defenses as it sweeps. Ice Beam is an alternative Ice-type STAB move that has higher Base Power than Freeze-Dry as well as more PP than Blizzard while being consistently accurate, making it more reliable against bulky teams. A Calm Mind + Draining Kiss set can be used to wear down bulkier structures while keeping Alolan Ninetales healthy; however, its low Special Attack means that it requires multiple boosts in order to properly muscle through defensive Pokemon like Umbreon.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: When Alolan Ninetales lacks Tera Blast Ground, defensive Steel-types like Registeel, Jirachi, and Empoleon can comfortably take hits from it before threatening it with a 4x super effective STAB move. More offensive Steel-types like Bisharp and Magnezone also threaten it; however, neither likes taking Nasty Plot-boosted attacks from Alolan Ninetales, and Bisharp risks being locked into Swords Dance or Sucker Punch by Encore.

Fire-types: Armarouge, Volcanion, and Entei resist both of Alolan Ninetales's STAB moves and can retaliate with super-effective STAB moves of their own. However, all three must be wary of Tera Blast Ground.

Faster Threats: Gengar and Maushold are able to comfortably outspeed Alolan Ninetales before either nailing it with their powerful attacks or crippling it with Trick or Encore. Choice Scarf Pokemon like Terrakion and Krookodile are also able to outspeed and revenge kill it.

Opposing Weather: In addition to being able to take Alolan Ninetales's attacks fairly comfortably, Politoed can prevent Aurora Veil from being set at all simply by switching in and replacing snow with rain. Hippowdon and Ninetales can also set sand or sun, respectively, in order to deny Aurora Veil; however, the former has difficulty switching in due to its Ice weakness, and the latter is a rather niche option.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
Set Details

Alolan Ninetales leverages its high Speed and rare offensive typing to act as an effective Nasty Plot sweeper that can dismantle common threats such as Cyclizar, Slowbro, and Krookodile. Freeze-Dry is a reliable STAB option that hits Water-types that could wall Alolan Ninetales otherwise for super effective damage like Gastrodon and Suicune. Blizzard is Alolan Ninetales's most powerful STAB move, notably guaranteeing an OHKO on Rhyperior after a Nasty Plot boost; however, it is much less accurate outside of snow. Encore can be used to cripple setup sweepers like Calm Mind Cresselia as well as utility Pokemon like Vaporeon, while Moonblast is a consistent STAB option that targets the likes of Umbreon and can KO Pokemon that would tank a Freeze-Dry like Krookodile or Galarian Zapdos after Stealth Rock damage. Tera Blast Ground patches up Alolan Ninetales's biggest offensive weaknesses, targeting Steel-types like Magnezone and Jirachi as well as Fire-types like Armarouge and Volcanion. Defensively, Tera Ground removes many of Alolan Ninetales's weaknesses, notably giving it a resistance to Rock-type attacks from the likes of Rhyperior and Terrakion as well as an immunity to Thunder Wave from Jirachi. However, Terastallizing removes the Defense boost snow provides, putting Alolan Ninetales at risk of being OHKOed by Mienshao's Close Combat.

Nasty Plot Alolan Ninetales fits best on bulky offense structures that can whittle down its checks. Entry hazard removal from the likes of Cyclizar and Talonflame ensure that Alolan Ninetales can come in safely even if its Heavy-Duty Boots is removed. Knock Off from the aforementioned Cyclizar as well as Krookodile can remove Leftovers from defensive Pokemon that lack reliable recovery, such as Hisuian Goodra and Registeel, as well as Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Volcanion and Entei, making them easier to wear down so that Alolan Ninetales can sweep late-game. Fighting- and Ground-types like Galarian Zapdos, Mienshao, and Krookodile also make for great partners by virtue of being able to threaten the Steel-types that otherwise check Alolan Ninetales while appreciating their ability to dispatch the most common weather setter in the tier: Hippowdon. Water-types like Crawdaunt and Basculegion-F appreciate Alolan Ninetales's ability to break past Grass-types such as Wo-Chien and Chesnaught; in exchange, they can threaten the Fire-types that resist its STAB combination like Armarouge. Barraskewda is another great Water-type partner for Alolan Ninetales, as it can threaten to KO faster Pokemon like Choice Scarf Krookodile thanks to its blistering Speed and access to Aqua Jet. Choice Scarf revenge killers, such as Jirachi and Krookodile, can similarly handle faster threats like Gengar in order to enable a sweep. Setup sweepers, like Bisharp and Gyarados, appreciate Alolan Ninetales's ability to create setup opportunities with Encore.

movesets.name: Aurora Veil
movesets.description:
Set Details

Alolan Ninetales provides both snow and support for its teammates, either granting protection with Aurora Veil or disrupting foes with Encore, enabling them to overwhelm the opposing team. Aurora Veil allows allies to set up with greater ease and protects them from retaliation. Encore can lock foes like Slowbro and Armarouge into setup moves like Calm Mind, healing moves like Slack Off, or other unfavorable moves, allowing Alolan Ninetales's teammates to enter the field unopposed. Snowscape can allow Alolan Ninetales to ensure the desired weather stays up in the face of other weather setters like Hippowdon and Politoed. Moonblast deals strong damage to Umbreon and Terrakion, while Freeze-Dry can hit Water-types like Slowbro and Gastrodon. Icy Rock extends the window that allied Pokemon can take advantage of Alolan Ninetales's Snow Warning. While Alolan Ninetales does not want to Terastallize often, preferring for its allies to make use of it, Tera Water flips its weaknesses to Fire and Steel, allowing it to survive attacks from Entei and Jirachi. In addition, it is a great defensive type and removes Alolan Ninetales's weakness to Stealth Rock, though losing its Ice typing will result in it no longer benefitting from snow's Defense boost.

Aurora Veil Alolan Ninetales fits almost exclusively on a single archetype: snow. As such, it should be paired with the most potent user of it, Belly Drum Cetitan, which often needs the protection provided by Aurora Veil in order to set up. Other Slush Rush sweepers like Alolan Sandslash and Beartic can also take advantage of the weather. Other Pokemon that benefit from snow are potential Weather Ball users like Volcanion, Raikou, and Kilowattrel, providing a means to damage Pokemon like Cyclizar and Chesnaught more effectively. Due to the low duration of Aurora Veil, Alolan Ninetales needs to be paired with pivots that can reliably get its allies in, a role that Eject Button Slowbro and Amoonguss can excel at. Entry hazard control is important for snow teams, which can come in the form of Defog Talonflame and Noivern or Rapid Spin Cyclizar, each of which can cover Alolan Ninetales's weakness to Fire and pivot with U-turn. Alternatively, Magic Bounce Espeon or Hattrem can prevent entry hazards from being set up at all, though their frailty can make them unreliable. Aurora Veil is also a benefit for any setup sweeper, even on non-snow teams, such as Gyarados and Armarouge.

strategies.overview: Snow Warning, great Speed, and a solid offensive typing distinguish Alolan Ninetales in roles as a support Pokemon and fast special attacker. Thanks to all these traits, Alolan Ninetales makes a great wallbreaker against Amoonguss and Vaporeon and a solid revenge killer against Flygon and Paldean Tauros-W. Snow helps Alolan Sandslash and Beartic to sweep, and Alolan Ninetales can lean into its snow setting by using Aurora Veil to support other dangerous setup sweepers like Scyther and Toxtricity. Snow even enables Alolan Ninetales itself, granting it a Defense boost and a perfectly accurate Blizzard. Alolan Ninetales is a good user of Terastallization to wallbreak more effectively, and it can quickly overwhelm supposed counterplay like Bronzong and Diancie. Unfortunately, Alolan Ninetales is walled by prominent Steel-types like Klefki, Bronzong, and Copperajah depending on its set and coverage, curtailing its own offensive presence. Fire-types like Chandelure, Incineroar, and Paldean Tauros-F are also troublesome for Alolan Ninetales, even if some of them don't resist Fairy. Despite snow mitigating Alolan Ninetales's poor Defense, physical attackers like Basculegion-M and Flamigo still hit Alolan Ninetales hard. Alolan Ninetales's Stealth Rock weakness makes its Heavy-Duty Boots sets vulnerable to Knock Off and disincentivizes running items besides Heavy-Duty Boots.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs may seem appealing, as Blizzard and Moonblast are quite spammable, but Alolan Ninetales becomes very dependent on entry hazard control without the same payoff in power as other special wallbreakers like Chandelure, Toxtricity, and Porygon-Z have. A set of Aurora Veil / Nasty Plot / Moonblast with one of Freeze-Dry, Blizzard, Tera Blast, or Dark Pulse can be used to wallbreak for snow and setup sweepers while also allowing them to set up more easily. Life Orb can be run over Heavy-Duty Boots to give Nasty Plot Alolan Ninetales variants enough power to OHKO offensive Incineroar most of the time with +2 Moonblast.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Bronzong and Copperajah totally wall Alolan Ninetales, and Klefki has Thunder Wave to slow down Nasty Plot Alolan Ninetales. However, all Steel-types must be wary of Encore from support sets and Tera Blast Fire, Ground, and, in Bronzong's case, Ghost from Nasty Plot variants.

Fire-types: Incineroar and Paldean Tauros-F threaten Alolan Ninetales offensively and can stomach its Ice-type attacks. Additionally, other Fire-types like Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion can completely wall Alolan Ninetales, tanking Moonblast as well as its Ice-type attacks. However, Paldean Tauros-F needs a Choice Scarf to outspeed Nasty Plot Alolan Ninetales so that it isn't OHKOed by its +2 Moonblast, and Tera Blast Ground can handle them all very easily.

Special Walls: Specially bulky Pokemon like Alolan Muk, Porygon2, and Diancie can tank boosted attacks from Alolan Ninetales and threaten it back with strong attacks or status.

movesets.name: Aurora Veil Support
movesets.description:
Set Details

Freeze-Dry is more threatening to prominent Water-types like Basculegion-M, Vaporeon, and Paldean Tauros-W. However, Blizzard hits more important KO thresholds, 2HKOing Cinccino, Amoonguss, and Toxtricity. Encore helps Alolan Ninetales lock passive Pokemon like Diancie and Alolan Muk into status moves, creating easier turns for setting up Aurora Veil. Foul Play can replace Moonblast to punish physical attackers like Basculegion-M, Steel-types, and Tera Steel Flygon, but it lacks Moonblast's superior coverage against Incineroar, Paldean Tauros-F, and Scrafty. Moonblast is also more important as coverage against Paldean Tauros-W if Alolan Ninetales drops Freeze-Dry for Blizzard. Icy Rock is more beneficial to teammates that rely on snow like Beartic and Alolan Sandslash, while Heavy-Duty Boots increase Alolan Ninetales's longevity in the face of entry hazards so that it can switch and set up snow more freely. Tera Water flips the Steel and Fire weaknesses into resistances, which is beneficial against Copperajah and Incineroar, and it gives Alolan Ninetales a generally good defensive typing with few weaknesses.

Alolan Sandslash and Beartic benefit most directly from Alolan Ninetales setting snow, and both of them enjoy Aurora Veil creating safer turns to set up Swords Dance. Aurora Veil also benefits setup sweepers that prefer multiple turns to fully set up like Scyther, Toxtricity, Scream Tail, Flygon, Paldean Tauros-F, and Double Dance Porygon-Z. Cinccino can keep entry hazards out of the picture with Tidy Up so that Alolan Ninetales can run Icy Rock, and Cinccino itself benefits from Aurora Veil mitigating its meager bulk and defensive utility. Diancie, Basculegion-M, and Paldean Tauros-W can check Fire-types like Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion that threaten Alolan Ninetales. Additionally, the first one can set hazards as well. Weather Ball users like Kilowattrel and Raikou can use snow set by Alolan Ninetales to benefit their coverage. Eject Button users like Galarian Slowbro and Amoonguss help Alolan Ninetales's teammates come onto the field safely to best take advantage of Alolan Ninetales's Aurora Veil.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
Set Details

Freeze-Dry's better effectiveness against bulky Water-types like Milotic and Vaporeon makes Alolan Ninetales an even more devastating wallbreaker than Blizzard would, but the greater power of Blizzard overwhelms special walls like Alolan Muk, Diancie, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro. Alolan Ninetales can use Encore over an Ice-type STAB or coverage move to facilitate itself as a setup sweeper by locking passive walls like Gastrodon, Porygon2, and Avalugg into useless status moves. Nasty Plot Alolan Ninetales greatly benefits from using Terastallilzation in conjunction with Tera Blast to surprise and overwhelm its checks. Tera Blast Ground beats Steel-types like Copperajah, Fire-types like Chandelure and Incineroar, and Poison-types like Alolan Muk and Galarian Slowbro. In addition, Tera Ground protects Alolan Ninetales from Thunder Wave users like Klefki and Porygon2, and it's a good defensive answer to Poison-type attacks from Alolan Muk and Munkidori while Alolan Ninetales sets up. Tera Blast Fire has similar offensive potency against Steel-types, and it's superior to Ground defensively against otherwise super effective Steel- and Fire-type attacks, though it makes Alolan Ninetales offensively weaker against Fire-types. Tera Ghost lets Alolan Ninetales use a Ghost-type Tera Blast to blow past Bronzong and Ghost-types like Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion. It also protects Alolan Ninetales from Cinccino as well as Speed-boosted Toxtricity and Porygon-Z for a critical turn, flips its Poison weakness against foes like Munkidori, and lets it take advantage of Body Press users like Avalugg and Bronzong. Dark Pulse covers Bronzong and Chandelure, and it's Alolan Ninetales's strongest attack against Galarian Slowbro and Munkidori if it lacks Blizzard. Tera Water offers Alolan Ninetales a convenient defensive typing to deal with its usual Fire and Steel weaknesses.

Alolan Ninetales makes for a good wallbreaker on offense and balance teams. Avalugg enjoys the Defense boost from snow, and along with walls like Cramorant and Altaria, it checks physical attackers like Flygon, Paldean Tauros-W, Infernape, and Scyther. Avalugg can also chip Steel-types like Bronzong and Copperajah and keep entry hazards off for Alolan Ninetales. Additionally, Altaria can run a Perish trap set to clear bothersome Steel- and Fire-types for Alolan Ninetales. Other hazard removers like Cinccino similarly chip Steel-types and can give Alolan Ninetales the freedom to run Life Orb. Ground-types like Flygon, Gastrodon, and Gligar can check Alolan Muk and pressure Fire-types and Steel-types besides Bronzong. Porygon2 and Incineroar are solid defensive answers to Hisuian Typhlosion and Chandelure, and the former can check Toxtricity, especially Choice Scarf variants, for Alolan Ninetales. Flygon, Fighting-types like Paldean Tauros-W, and Fire-types like Paldean Tauros-F can put the pressure on Steel-types like Klefki, Copperajah, and Bronzong so that Alolan Ninetales can finish them off late-game.

movesets.name: Snow Support (Ice)
movesets.description:
Alolan Ninetales is a great support Pokemon for Ice teams thanks to its ability to set snow and Aurora Veil to make its team much harder to take down and facilitate its teammates' sweeping attempts with Encore. In addition, its typing and Speed tier let it hit otherwise troublesome Fighting-types such as Keldeo, Urshifu-R, and Great Tusk. Freeze-Dry is useful against Water teams, being able to threaten Pelipper and Quagsire out and dissuade Pelipper from setting rain in its face in an attempt to stop Aurora Veil. Moonblast is useful against the ubiquitous Fighting- and Dragon-types in the tier, as it hits Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Scrafty, and Raging Bolt that are otherwise problems for Ice teams. Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to lock a defensive Pokemon, such as Toxapex, into a weak move or a setup sweeper, such as Swords Dance Iron Hands or Bulk Up Ursaluna, into a stat-boosting move, letting Alolan Ninetales's teammates take care of the aforementioned Pokemon. Icy Rock is used for extending snow turns for the team, particularly assisting allies with snow-related abilities, while Light Clay can be used to extend the amount of time Aurora Veil is up for, supporting its more specially frail teammates for longer.

Mamoswine can threaten Fire-types like Heatran, Torkoal, and Cinderace with Earthquake while packing Thick Fat for a pseudo-Fire neutrality. Additionally, it sets Stealth Rock, which can help Alolan Ninetales pick off weakened threats such as Kyurem. Cetitan is a great partner, as Slush Rush allows it to outspeed and OHKO most of the metagame after a Belly Drum boost, which is easier to acquire thanks to snow and Aurora Veil from Alolan Ninetales. Alolan Sandslash appreciates snow and Aurora Veil both bolstering its bulk and Slush Rush doubling its Speed, allowing it to threaten Fire-, Steel-, and Poison-types like Iron Moth, Iron Treads, and pre-Unburden Sneasler with Earthquake. In exchange, Alolan Sandslash can use Rapid Spin to clear entry hazards and deal with Hatterene and Flutter Mane, which can both take advantage of Alolan Ninetales. Cloyster is a threatening Shell Smash sweeper that can take out threats to Ice like Ogerpon-H and Ceruledge with Rock Blast and has a high Defense stat that makes it nearly unbreakable in snow. In return, Alolan Ninetales facilitates Cloyster's Shell Smash setup thanks to Aurora Veil and snow support. Cloyster also appreciates Alolan Ninetales locking its defensive answers, such as Toxapex, into unfavorable moves. Kyurem is a good offensive teammate that breaks down walls like Archaludon with snow-assisted Blizzards and breaks down Water-types like Toxapex and Swampert with Freeze-Dry. Snow and Aurora Veil also make it significantly harder to revenge kill. Avalugg is a defensive behemoth that, when under snow and Aurora Veil, takes on almost every physical attacker in the tier. It can also remove Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin to improve Alolan Ninetales's lacking longevity. Finally, Frosmoth becomes a dangerous sweeping threat under snow and Aurora Veil thanks to Quiver Dance, letting it potentially win the Ground, Flying, and Fairy matchups.

movesets.name: Snow Setter
movesets.description:
• Alolan Ninetales is the premier snow setter due to its Speed tier and utility. It enables offensive structures that flourish with Aurora Veil support, reducing damage from opposing Pokemon.
  • Alolan Ninetales runs Freeze-Dry in order to force super effective damage on prominent Water-types like Ogerpon-W.
  • Icy Wind is a strong speed control option that allows Alolan Ninetales and its teammates to outpace Chien-Pao and Ogerpon formes. Blizzard can be brought over Icy Wind as a stronger STAB option, allowing it to guarantee a OHKO on Landorus.
  • Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to deter setup from Pokemon like Calm Mind Raging Bolt and bulky Swords Dance Ogerpon-W, which is normally threatening for Alolan Ninetales and its teammates, as well as locking opposing Pokemon like Incineroar and Iron Hands into Fake Out. Moonblast is a secondary STAB option that allows it to hit Incineroar for neutral damage and Chien-Pao for super effective damage. Protect can be chosen to aid Alolan Ninetales in preserving itself to reset snow later.
  • The bulk investment on Alolan Ninetales allows it to survive two Hard Stone-boosted Diamond Storms from Adamant Diancie when behind Aurora Veil and Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-C without Aurora Veil support.
  • The Speed and Special Attack investment allows Alolan Ninetales to outspeed and OHKO Landorus with Blizzard or Freeze-Dry.
  • Tera Ghost is the premier Tera type on Alolan Ninetales due to the Fake Out immunity, allowing it to drop Protect and ensure that Aurora Veil is set up, while also providing a Fighting-type immunity from threats like Iron Hands and a resistance to Glimmora's and Landorus's Sludge Bombs.
  • Teams with Alolan Ninetales often play very offensively, benefitting from the extra bulk that its Aurora Veil provides by enabling setup threats like Raging Bolt, Galarian Moltres, and Kingambit. Kyurem is often Alolan Ninetales's best partner, as it benefits from the snow's Defense boost and an accurate Blizzard.
  • Alolan Ninetales appreciates a strong Fake Out user, like Iron Hands or Incineroar, to allow it to set up Aurora Veil more freely.
  • Alolan Ninetales appreciates Landorus, Iron Hands, Ogerpon-W, and Okidogi because they can offensively threaten prolific Steel- and Fire-types such as Gholdengo, Ogerpon-H, and Incineroar, which check Alolan Ninetales.

strategies.outdated: With the advent of Regulation G allowing restricted Pokemon, Battle Stadium Singles is going through a huge shakeup! This analysis is currently outdated and covers Regulation F, so not all the information here will be relevant to the current metagame.
strategies.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.
strategies.comments:
Speed EV Benchmarks

  • Alolan Ninetales should almost always use a Timid nature, as this is the most efficient way for it to outspeed a wide variety of threats.

  • 60+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Adamant Urshifu formes.

  • 68+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Modest Iron Crown.

  • 84+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Modest Chi-Yu.

  • 116+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Jolly Landorus-T, Jolly Annihilape, and Jolly Gouging Fire.

  • 156+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Adamant Ogerpon formes and Modest Latios.

  • 164+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Jolly Urshifu formes.

  • 172+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Timid Iron Crown.

  • 188+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Timid Chi-Yu and Jolly Entei.

  • 204+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Jolly Garchomp.

  • 220+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Adamant Roaring Moon.

  • 244+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Adamant Meowscarada.

Defensive EV Benchmarks

  • 244 HP / 108 SpD EVs: This survives Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast.

  • 244 HP / 92 SpD EVs: This has a 93.7% chance of surviving Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast.

  • 180 HP / 244 Def EVs: This avoids a 2HKO from Adamant Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and almost always avoids an OHKO from Scizor's unboosted Bullet Punch.

  • 196 HP / 244 Def EVs: This spread is not OHKOed by Adamant Scizor's Bullet Punch if it lacks an offensive item, and it is also not 2HKOed by Adamant Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes.

  • 148 HP / 180 SpD EVs: This is the most efficient EV spread for surviving Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast at the cost of serious physical bulk.

movesets.name: Screens Setter
movesets.description:
• With the new Defense-boosting mechanic for Ice-types in snow, Alolan Ninetales is the premier screens setter in the current metagame, as well as being a decent check against fearsome physical attackers like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R.

  • Encore: Encore can thwart bulkier setup foes that would otherwise take advantage of Alolan Ninetales's mediocre offenses.

  • Blizzard versus Freeze-Dry: Blizzard's high Base Power helps make up for Alolan Ninetales's lack of power. Freeze-Dry is much less powerful but is more consistent at pressuring Water-types like Ogerpon-W and Basculegion-M.

  • Pain Split: Pain Split punishes foes that assume Alolan Ninetales will simply allow revenge kills from slower Pokemon, giving it a new lease on life to check physical threats. This especially works well with Rocky Helmet.

Other Options
  • Misty Terrain: Misty Terrain stops common users of status such as Yawn Ursaluna-B and Thunder Wave Porygon2 from having an impact, though it does weaken grounded Dragon-type teammates like Raging Bolt and Roaring Moon.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Thanks to its high Speed and increased physical bulk in snow, Alolan Ninetales does not normally want to Terastallize. It's true it can help with Steel-types moves from Scizor and Choice Scarf Gholdengo, but it is often more advisable to play around this weakness through its teammates.

  • Water: Tera Water is a balanced defensive typing that completely flips Alolan Ninetales's Steel-type weakness, all but guaranteeing it can set Aurora Veil. It also lets it resist Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes—a common counter against screens—though Alolan Ninetales will normally survive it without Terastallizing.

  • Fire: Tera Fire can be used offensively and defensively against Steel-types, with invested Tera Blast usually OHKOing Scizor and 2HKOing Gholdengo. Do note though that this comes at the cost of having a dramatically worse Urshifu-R matchup.

  • Ice: Tera Ice lets Alolan Ninetales keep its Defense boost in snow while increasing its offensive output and making the devastating Steel weakness more manageable.

Items

  • Light Clay: Light Clay extends Aurora Veil's duration and makes it much harder for the opponent to play around it.

  • Rocky Helmet: If using a physically defensive EV spread, Rocky Helmet lets Alolan Ninetales severely punish Urshifu-R that lack Punching Glove.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash is good insurance against fast super effective hits, but it's overall less useful in the majority of matchups.

EV Spread Examples

  • Alolan Ninetales has a wide variety of possible EV spreads. If the examples below don't suit your needs, consider checking out some useful Speed and Defensive benchmarks later in this analysis to help create a custom EV spread!

  • 244 HP / 92 SpD / 172 Spe with Timid: This spread lets Alolan Ninetales outspeed up to Timid Iron Crown and Jolly Urshifu formes while surviving Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera-boosted Moonblast on all but the highest damage roll.

  • 228 HP / 76 Def / 4 SpA / 116 SpD / 84 Spe with Timid: With this investment in bulk, Alolan Ninetales survives Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast, as well as avoiding an OHKO from Ogerpon-H's super effective Ivy Cudgel while the weather is still snow. The Speed investment lets Alolan Ninetales outrun Modest Chi-Yu.

  • 180 HP / 140 SpD / 188 Spe with Timid: This spread sacrifices some physical bulk in exchange for outspeeding Timid Chi-Yu and almost always survives Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera-boosted Moonblast.

  • 180 HP / 244 Def / 84 Spe with Timid: This physically bulky spread avoids a 2HKO from Adamant Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes while outspeeding up to Modest Chi-Yu. It also avoids an OHKO from Scizor's unboosted Bullet Punch on all but the highest damage roll.

strategies.overview:
• Weather control in Snow Warning and Aurora Veil support give Alolan Ninetales a strong niche in the metagame. Alolan Ninetales's great offensive typing allows it to threaten Chien-Pao, Urshifu-S, and Landorus with an OHKO while also walling the former two.

  • Alolan Ninetales pairs especially well with slower Ice-types that appreciate the added bulk from snow, such as Articuno and Baxcalibur. Hisuian Arcanine also makes for an excellent partner, helping Alolan Ninetales set up Aurora Veil through Intimidate support, dishing out great damage, and threatening Ice-resistant foes, such as Gholdengo, Incineroar, and Kingambit. All of these partners have fantastic offensive pressure through setup or Choice items, making up for Alolan Ninetales's poor offenses. Ogerpon-W does a great job at helping set up Aurora Veil with Follow Me and threatening foes that resist Ice-type moves like Incineroar with Ivy Cudgel.

  • Alolan Ninetales struggles against opposing weather setters such as Tornadus, which can shut down the snow composition. Fire- and Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Chi-Yu are threats, as they resist Ninetales-Alola's and Articuno's Ice-type STAB moves, as well as ignoring Ogerpon-W's Follow Me through Make It Rain and Heat Wave.

movesets.name: Screen Setter
movesets.description:
• Moonblast guarantees a 2HKO on Urshifu-R. Helping Hand helps make up for Alolan Ninetales's poor damage output.

  • Light Clay is used to make sure Aurora Veil lasts for the majority of the game.

  • The defensive investment allows Alolan Ninetales to survive Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast and avoid the 2HKO from Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel and Rillaboom's Wood Hammer, while the Speed investment allows it to outspeed Landorus.

  • Tera Fire allows Alolan Ninetales to resist the Fire- and Steel-type moves that otherwise give it trouble, such as Gholdengo's Make it Rain and Ogerpon-H's STAB moves.

strategies.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Alolan Ninetales heavily struggles against Gholdengo, being unable to punish it with Encore or threaten it with its STAB moves. Fire-types like Incineroar, Hisuian Arcanine, and Volcarona put pressure on Alolan Ninetales while shrugging off all of its attacks. Opposing weather control like Tyranitar and Torkoal are also major issues, making Alolan Ninetales's Blizzard inaccurate and Aurora Veil useless.
  • Dragonite works well with both sets, providing speed control and taking on the Fire-types Alolan Ninetales is weak to, especially with Stomping Tantrum.
  • Offensive Alolan Ninetales is strongest with other offensive threats to overwhelm the opposing team with Pokemon that cover each other's checks. The most notable of these are Sneasler and Kingambit. Sneasler can threaten Incineroar for a lot of damage and has a faster Fake Out but struggles to damage Dragonite and Gholdengo. Alolan Ninetales can cover for Dragonite and Kingambit can take on Gholdengo.
  • Screens setter Alolan Ninetales works best alongside multiple setup sweepers that can steal the game when supported well. Annihilape and Gholdengo cannot be slowed down by Fake Out and hit the majority of the metagame for great damage. Annihilape and Gholdengo also notably take care of Incineroar and Sneasler, two of Alolan Ninetales's toughest matchups.

Strategy Comments

  • Offensive Alolan Ninetales's primary role is as a fast sweeper with unique support options. It is best when dishing out early damage while being supported by Fake Out or redirection and going down after taking on what it's expected to handle so Alolan Ninetales's teammates can clean up. Screens setter Alolan Ninetales is strongest when it sets up screens for its team and faints soon after, ensuring its teammates can take full advantage of the Aurora Veil turns and being not nearly as passive.
  • Offensive Alolan Ninetales's flexibility allows it to be an excellent lead Pokemon, threatening foes with powerful Blizzards, Icy Wind speed control, and often Aurora Veil support. This lets it adapt in many lead matchups and position itself in a way to win the game. Choice Specs Alolan Ninetales also plays similarly, as its damage output is rather forceful from turn 1. After Alolan Ninetales impacts the game, it's good to send out your other offensive Pokemon that can finish the job most efficiently. Screens setter Alolan Ninetales also finds itself as a lead, but for different reasons. Alolan Ninetales can use its many support options to set the board for sweepers like Gholdengo and Annihilape to come in and set up. Alolan Ninetales may want to Terastallize if opposing Pokemon threaten to KO it before it sets up Aurora Veil or when interested in sticking around for Icy Wind and Encore support.
  • Gholdengo is Alolan Ninetales's most reliable answer, as Alolan Ninetales cannot threaten it or lock it into a move with Encore. Alolan Ninetales is also 4x weak to Make It Rain and weak to Shadow Ball after Terastallizing into a Ghost-type. Tyranitar is also a great counter, overriding weather and passively breaking Alolan Ninetales's Focus Sash. It's wise to use Kingambit and Annihilape to threaten these Pokemon while preserving Alolan Ninetales, by switching it out once its checks enter the field.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description:
• Offensive Alolan Ninetales is a good Pokemon in Regulation H thanks to its fast STAB Blizzard in snow, threatening metagame staples like Rillaboom, Dragonite, and the Ursaluna formes, and its ability to support its team in a pinch thanks to its wide supportive movepool.
  • Freeze-Dry grants Alolan Ninetales the ability to threaten Basculegion-M and the plethora of Tera Water Pokemon in the format, such as Gholdengo and Amoonguss. Aurora Veil is a great move to increase the team's longevity when Alolan Ninetales can't do a lot on the field or take advantage of defensive play. Encore can be used over these two to better punish defensive play and discourage Fake Out, especially if Alolan Ninetales does not carry Protect. Moonblast and Dazzling Gleam are great secondary STAB moves on Choice Specs variants, threatening 2HKOs on Kingambit and Annihilape, respectively, and ensuring Alolan Ninetales doesn't get walled by Incineroar. Icy Wind is preferred over Protect to provide Alolan Ninetales with speed control.
  • Focus Sash is preferred to get around Alolan Ninetales's poor defensive typing, Choice Specs and Never-Melt Ice sacrifice longevity for better damage rolls against the metagame; Choice Specs Blizzard OHKOes Ursaluna-B and Never-Melt Ice Blizzard guarantees a 2HKO on uninvested Archaludon not holding an Assault Vest.
  • Alolan Ninetales prefers Tera Ghost across all its sets, as it provides an immunity to Fake Out and sheds all of its weaknesses. Alolan Ninetales can utilize Tera Ice as well, ensuring even Ursaluna gets OHKOed by Choice Specs Alolan Ninetales. Focus Sash and Never-Melt Ice Alolan Ninetales can OHKO uninvested and bulky Ursaluna-B, respectively, with Tera Ice Blizzard.
  • Offensive Alolan Ninetales can provide much more offensive pressure but has longevity issues with the plethora of Fake Out and its weaknesses in the metagame.

movesets.name: Screens Setter
movesets.description:
• Alolan Ninetales also finds a good niche as a supportive screens setter thanks to its good Speed tier and access to a variety of other support tools.
  • This Alolan Ninetales focuses more on setting up Aurora Veil and disrupting with Encore so its team can set up and sweep more comfortably rather than threatening bulky Pokemon itself.
  • Covert Cloak is preferred to provide Alolan Ninetales with an immunity to Fake Out and Speed drops from Electabuzz's Electroweb. Light Clay sacrifices this for screens to stay up longer, allowing for more setup opportunities and room to position Alolan Ninetales's teammates.
  • Alolan Ninetales uses Tera Water to improve its defensive profile, turning the glaring Steel- and Fire-type weaknesses into resistances. Light Clay sets may use Tera Ghost to keep the potential Fake Out immunity. Both Tera types remove all of Alolan Ninetales's original weaknesses.
  • The EV spread ensures that Alolan Ninetales survives Sneasler's Tera Stellar Dire Claw and Life Orb Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon. The Speed investment allows Alolan Ninetales to outspeed Indeedee-M and Hisuian Typhlosion, while the Special Attack ensures a 2HKO on Ursaluna-B.
  • Screens setter Alolan Ninetales can last a lot longer on the field to use its support kit, but it is easier to ignore in the majority of matchups due to its lackluster damage output.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 5 onwards

Price Range: 9-11 points

Overview: Alolan Ninetales carves itself a niche in the format as the premier Aurora Veil setter while also being a solid utility Pokemon. Thanks to its great Speed tier, it can reliably set Aurora Veil while also supporting its teammates with strong support moves and providing snow for Ice-types. It also has access to Nasty Plot alongside solid STAB moves to make it a passable wallbreaker against certain teams. Its major drawbacks are that it has mediocre offensive stats and a very debilitating Steel weakness, and it's also directly outclassed by a lot of other Pokemon for the roles it wants to fill, notably lacking pivoting, which makes it hard to safely bring in teammates that benefit from Aurora Veil. However, it does compress roles that other Pokemon do not, meaning that it can be a strong choice on certain builds.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Utility: Alolan Ninetales is blessed with one of the strongest utility movepools in the metagame, primarily setting Aurora Veil for its teammates but also using moves such as Encore, Hypnosis, and Foul Play, all of which can help swing the tide of games back into the user's favor by crippling not just offensive but also defensive threats.

Setup: While far less common, Nasty Plot Alolan Ninetales can be used despite its middling Special Attack thanks to having strong STAB moves in Blizzard and Moonblast and solid enough coverage options to muscle through some of its would-be checks. It does run into issues with Steel-types, but it can also muscle through most.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Blizzard, Freeze-Dry, Moonblast, Draining Kiss

Setup Moves: Nasty Plot, Calm Mind, Agility

Utility Moves: Aurora Veil, Encore, Hypnosis, Foul Play, Disable, Pain Split, Roar

Coverage: Dark Pulse, Extrasensory, Hex, Psyshock, Tera Blast

Niche Moves

Snowscape: Snowscape allows Alolan Ninetales to keep snow up against opposing weather setters, which could otherwise switch in to prevent Aurora Veil.

Charm: Lowering the foe's Attack can allow one of Alolan Ninetales's allies an even easier opportunity to set up.

Imprison: Alolan Ninetales can prevent opposing Pokemon from using its snow to set their own Aurora Veil by using Imprison. This can be most impactful against offensively oriented teams.

Icy Wind: Icy Wind provides Alolan Ninetales with a helpful form of speed control, slowing down foes to allow its teammates to outspeed them once it faints. It can also prevent Speed-boosting setup sweepers from getting out of hand.

Common Items

Light Clay: Light Clay extending the duration of Aurora Veil can give teammates the extra turns needed to safely enter the field and set up. It's incredibly helpful when using frailer setup Pokemon, as they usually need to be brought in via a slow pivot.

Heavy-Duty Boots: The go-to item for most Pokemon with a Stealth Rock weakness, Heavy-Duty Boots gives Alolan Ninetales longevity to make it useful throughout the entire course of the game.

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: In scenarios where Alolan Ninetales may struggle to set Aurora Veil, resistance Berries can sometimes provide it the single free turn that it may need.

Damage-boosting Items: Both Choice Specs and Life Orb can be strong options in the right matchups, but they both run the risk of making Alolan Ninetales held back by entry hazards to the point where it's almost impossible to use them without strong hazard removal.

Mental Herb: To circumvent fast Encore and Taunt users, Alolan Ninetales can use Mental Herb, giving it a free turn to Aurora Veil.

Focus Sash: While nearly always outclassed by Light Clay and Mental Herb, Focus Sash can help on sacrificial lead sets that otherwise may be picked off by Bullet Punch or Choice Scarf users.

Eject Button: One way to circumvent Alolan Ninetales's lack of pivoting is by using Eject Button, giving it a free switch out after setting Aurora Veil. It can also still be useful even if Aurora Veil hasn't been set, as it grants safe entry for Ice-types and Slush Rush users alike.

Tera

Alolan Ninetales does not benefit from Tera much at all in its primary role as utility support; it appreciates the natural Defense boost from snow too much to want to lose it from using Tera. Where it does appreciate Tera is on offensive sets, with Tera types such as Tera Ground and Fighting giving it strong coverage options, Tera Water and Steel giving it easier setup opportunities, and Tera Fire achieving both. The rare Tera Ice can also be used to buff the damage of Blizzard even further. It does not need Tera to perform its roles, but it can make for a solid secondary Tera Captain, especially when it's priced at 9 points.

Draft Strategy

Alolan Ninetales is primarily used as a support option on offensive builds and thus shouldn't be considered unless teams fit most, if not all, of the following criteria. Teams also usually opt for better snow setters like Galarian Slowking and dual screens setters with better utility or pivoting like Grimmsnarl unless they explicitly need Alolan Ninetales's role compression.

Strong Setup: Aurora Veil makes setup considerably easier for all Pokemon, and a team should have multiple strong setup options before considering Alolan Ninetales, with some examples being Ogerpon-W, Greninja, and Iron Valiant. Alolan Ninetales also has notably strong synergy with Ice-types such as Baxcalibur and Kyurem, with its snow giving them a further Defense boost to enable setup even more.

Entry Hazard Control: Both Alolan Ninetales and its teammates do not want to have to run Heavy-Duty Boots unless absolutely necessary, while they also benefit massively from entry hazards consistently being up on the opponent's side. Pokemon such as Gliscor and Hisuian Samurott can be effective hazard setters, while Blastoise and Talonflame can be strong, offensive hazard removers. A handful of Pokemon like Iron Treads and Donphan can also do both.

Slow Momentum: Since Alolan Ninetales lacks momentum-grabbing moves, it can't safely get frailer teammates onto the field, which is why it benefits from pairing with teammates with slow pivoting such as Corviknight, Scizor, and Iron Hands.

Ghost-types: One of the most common ways to stop Aurora Veil is to remove it with Brick Break. Ghost-types such as Ceruledge and Brambleghast can make for solid teammates, since they're entirely immune to Brick Break. Gholdengo especially makes for a great option, as it also prevents Defog, another common way to remove Aurora Veil.

Checks and Counters

Dual Screens Removal: Alolan Ninetales's primary use is for Aurora Veil, and there are many ways to consistently remove it, ranging from Brick Break and Psychic Fangs, which destroy it, to Defog, which removes it alongside any entry hazards set by Alolan Ninetales's teammates.

Opposing Weather: Opposing weather setters, both via abilities and manual setting, can prevent Alolan Ninetales from setting Aurora Veil simply by switching into it on the turn it uses Aurora Veil or outspeeding it, respectively.

Entry Hazards: Since Alolan Ninetales wants to run Light Clay or other items that aid in setting up Aurora Veil frequently, it finds itself susceptible to entry hazards, notably Stealth Rock, which can be set against it for free by Steel-types such as Heatran, Tinkaton, and Metagross.

Steel-types: Utility sets, especially without Tera, find themselves shut down by most Steel-types, being forced into other teammates that may not want to take status or disruption moves. Bullet Punch, which is learned by a decent number of Steel-types, can also threaten to OHKO Alolan Ninetales before it can even set Aurora Veil.

movesets.name: Aurora Veil
movesets.description: Alolan Ninetales is a decent lead in Ubers UU thanks to having Aurora Veil, a good Speed stat and typing, and useful utility options. Although Freeze-Dry is normally the preferred STAB move because it hits Water-types like Palafin and Walking Wake, Blizzard can be used instead for its greater power. Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to take advantage of opposing leads and setup sweepers attempting to set up entry hazards or use it as setup fodder like Nasty Plot Mewtwo and Dragon Dance Arceus formes. Hypnosis is an option instead, allowing Alolan Ninetales to decommission these foes by putting them to sleep. Although Alolan Ninetales doesn't Terastallize often, Tera Water can be used to flip the matchup against Chi-Yu, Gholdengo, and Ogerpon-H, allowing it to set up Aurora Veil in front of them. Alolan Ninetales fits best on hyper offense teams looking for a dedicated lead to set up Aurora Veil to make their attackers more potent. Setup sweepers like Kingambit, Chien-Pao, and Baxcalibur all appreciate the Aurora Veil Alolan Ninetales sets up, with the latter two also benefitting from the Defense boost from snow. Pokemon like Landorus and Zamazenta-C that can deal with the Fire-, Steel-, and Poison-types Alolan Ninetales can struggle to set up Aurora Veil against are good partners.

movesets.name: Encore + Disable
movesets.description:
• Protect, Encore, and Disable are all used in conjunction to shut down slower foes and make them use Struggle twice, while Moonblast provides the remaining damage. Encore also can be used to lock foes into status moves.
  • Generally, Protect is used on turn 1. In response to a foe's move, Encore can be used to continually lock it into a status move and slowly KO it with Moonblast. Encore can also lock the foe into a relatively weak attacking move; Alolan Ninetales can then use Protect into Disable into Encore again to force the foe to take two turns of Struggle.
  • Alternatively after using Protect on turn 1, Disable can be used on a Choice-locked Pokemon or a potentially dangerous move from a non-Choice-locked Pokemon. If the foe used that move again, Encore can be used right away, but if it used a different move, Protect is used again on turn 3, then Encore, then Protect, then Disable, and then Encore to then trigger two turns of Struggle.
  • If additional damage is needed, Moonblast can also be used on turn 2, assuming the foe will swap moves to avoid Disable.
  • If an opponent is faster, but is unable to KO Alolan Ninetales with the combination of two attacks and two uses of Struggle after Leftovers recovery, Alolan Ninetales can still lock it into two turns of Struggle by using Encore first and using Disable immediately afterward.
  • Moonblast does the most damage after the foe's Struggle damage and has the added bonus of being able to KO Urshifu-S, which would otherwise bypass Protect thanks to its ability.
  • Leftovers provides passive healing over multiple turns, which lets Alolan Ninetales survive multiple hits and Struggles.
  • Maximum Speed lets Alolan Ninetales beat many slower Pokemon thanks to Encore and Disable while also Speed tying with non-Speed Booster Walking Wake. Its HP investment allows Alolan Ninetales to survive unboosted Sylveon's Hyper Beam, and the Defense investment gives it good odds to survive Choice Scarf Great Tusk's Head Smash.
  • Alolan Ninetales struggles with faster Pokemon like Choice Scarf Haxorus and Choice Scarf Porygon-Z, so it pairs well with bulky Pokemon that are able to survive hits from these foes, such as Metagross.
  • Alolan Ninetales also struggles with Pokemon that run multiple powerful moves that it can't survive, like Metagross, Skeledirge, and Life Orb Porygon-Z, and naturally pairs well with Pokemon like Urshifu-S and Ursaluna.

movesets.name: Aurora Veil (Ice)
movesets.description: With access to Snow Warning and Aurora Veil, a great typing, and a key Speed tier that lets it deal with the likes of Keldeo and Urshifu-R, Alolan Ninetales proves to be extremely useful for Ice teams. Freeze-Dry makes it a menace in the Water matchup, dealing heavy damage to Swampert, Gastrodon, and Pelipper. Encore enables Alolan Ninetales to disrupt walls and slower setup sweepers like Ting-Lu and Tapu Fini. Alolan Ninetales's teammates appreciate its supportive capabilities; setup sweepers like Swords Dance Weavile and Dragon Dance Baxcalibur have a lot more setup opportunities, and offensive Pokemon like Galarian Darmanitan have an easier time switching in. Cloyster is a stellar partner; its defensive set removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin and sets Spikes to wear down Keldeo and Toxapex for Alolan Ninetales, while Shell Smash variants can more easily set up with its assistance. SubRoost Kyurem helps Alolan Ninetales pressure Water teams with its own Freeze-Dry and checks Fighting-types like Galarian Zapdos with a Chople Berry. Piloswine lays down Stealth Rock and switches into and checks a variety of Fire-types that Alolan Ninetales hates, such as Volcarona and Iron Moth.
